card.title: Exam bank — every board question on rate of heat flow

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions: heater rate (2023: 4200 J in 4 s = 1050 W) and rate definition with formula plus unit (2022). Rate means joule per second (watt); conduction follows K A dT/L; black bodies radiate sigma T^4.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: rate = Q/t (W) · conduction Q/t = K A dT/L · Stefan E = sigma T4, sigma = 5.67x10^-8

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Conduction needs steady state (linear gradient, meaning no heat stored in the rod). K measurement assumes one-dimensional insulated flow. Stefan needs kelvin and black (or grey-with-e) surfaces.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 4200/4 = 1050 W. Doubling kelvin multiplies radiation 16x (T4 leverage). Metals conduct via free electrons; trapped air insulates (wool, fur).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): 4200/4 = 1050 J/s = 1050 W. NEB 2022 (2): rate defined as heat per unit time with Q/t and watt. Conduction variant reads K from the same formula rearranged.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: rate confused with quantity (watt vs joule); Celsius in Stefan law; linear conduction assumed past steady state. Real bodies are grey, not black.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: K from Searle bar: steady flow through known A, L, dT gives K = (Q/t) L/A dT (calorimeter measures Q/t at the cold end). Stefan is empirical with thermodynamic backing from Planck.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Rate' always means divide by time, answer in watts. Conduction: write K A dT/L and solve the fraction. T4: kelvin first, always.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): 4200 J in 4 s rate + unit. NEB 2022 (2): rate definition + formula + unit. That is the complete bank.
